key.name: mode
key.description: low = 30 Hz, standard = 60 Hz, medium = 90 Hz, high = 120 Hz (the panel default); adaptive = 120 Hz while touched, adaptive-idle-rate when idle (needs the panel runtime rate; else like high). A mode the kernel does not offer falls back to the next lower rate.

key.name: adaptive-idle-rate
key.description: Settings offers 60, 30 and 10; other values round down to one of them. 60 keeps 60 fps video smooth; 30 and 10 save more on a still screen.

key.name: adaptive-idle-ms
key.summary: Adaptive: idle after this many ms without touch or keys

key.name: saver-cap
key.summary: Battery saver limits the refresh rate to 60 Hz

key.name: smooth-mode
key.summary: Mode the quick-settings tile switches on
key.description: The last mode above 60 Hz chosen in Settings. The tile toggles between it and standard.

key.name: confirmed
key.summary: The current mode was confirmed by the user
key.description: Settings clears this while a new mode is on trial and sets it on "Keep" or when going back. If the shell starts with an unconfirmed mode, it goes back to high.

key.name: confirmed-modes
key.description: The quick-settings tile only switches to these without asking; for others it opens Settings.

key.name: available-rates
key.summary: Refresh rates of the built-in display's modes (written by the shell)
key.description: Comma-separated, ascending, e.g. 30,60,90,120. Empty until the shell has started.

key.name: adaptive-available
key.summary: The panel supports a runtime rate (written by the shell)

key.name: active-rate
key.summary: Refresh rate in use (written by the shell)
